rule: How LTM can help for FinOps IQ (WS-S5; DESIGN.md 11; PLAN F9). Generic practice names only; providers and tools appear only as options chosen from the client's requirements, with alternatives. No partner claims. The client sees type, purpose and execution outline; indicative scope appears only in the consultant's SOW draft (D7). The text reads as advice, never as a sales pitch.

offerings.name: FinOps assessment and value validation
offerings.purpose: Confirm the capability profile and turn indicative value into evidenced ranges with your own billing data.
outline: Validate the capability profile with billing data (FOCUS exports where available) and provider-tool recommendations
Confirm answers given as "Don't know" and facts left blank
Turn levers identified but not quantified into evidenced ranges
Agree capability targets with you

offerings.name: FinOps operating model and governance
offerings.purpose: Make someone accountable for technology spend, with a mandate, a cadence and policies that hold.
outline: Charter and executive sponsor
Responsibilities across engineering, finance and procurement
Review cadence, KPI set and policy set
Education plan, and links to IT asset management, IT financial management, security and sustainability

offerings.name: FinOps data, allocation and tooling implementation
offerings.purpose: Give every cost an accountable owner and complete, timely data on the platforms you use.
outline: Central cost data pipeline in FOCUS format
Allocation rules and account hierarchy; tag and label policy as code
Dashboards for each persona and anomaly alerts routed to owners
Tool selection from your requirements, with alternatives

offerings.name: Optimisation sprints
offerings.purpose: Realise the lever value with changes your engineers accept, verified against billing data.
outline: A backlog for each lever and platform: idle clean-up, scheduling, rightsizing, storage lifecycle, Spot adoption, commitment portfolio

outline.text: Kubernetes requests and limits tuned to measured use

outline: Changes made with performance guardrails
Savings verified against billing data before and after

offerings.name: Unit economics, forecasting and chargeback
offerings.purpose: Tie spend to business output, forecast it from its drivers and charge it to the units that use it.
outline: Unit metric design with product owners
Product telemetry joined to allocation data in business intelligence
Driver-based forecast
Showback, then chargeback into the ERP

offerings.name: Managed FinOps service
offerings.purpose: Run the practice while your own capability grows, where internal capacity is limited.
outline: Ongoing allocation hygiene and commitment portfolio management
Anomaly response, monthly reviews and KPI reporting
Capability handed back to you over time

offerings.name: Workload placement and cost-aware architecture
offerings.purpose: Place workloads where they cost least for what they need, and remove cost built into the architecture.
outline: Placement decisions across public cloud, private cloud and data centre with a cost model
Architecture reviews for data transfer and modernisation
Migration or re-platforming where the business case supports it

offerings.name: AI cost and value management
offerings.purpose: Know what each AI use case costs and keep GPU and inference spend in line with its value.
outline: GPU utilisation and idle-endpoint controls
Token and inference cost attributed to each use case
Model-choice reviews for cost and quality

offerings.name: SaaS portfolio and vendor strategy
offerings.purpose: Rationalise the SaaS and software portfolio and set the strategy for the largest vendors, beyond licence clean-up.
outline: Portfolio review: overlapping tools and usage against entitlements
Renewal and negotiation strategy for the largest contracts
Consolidation plan agreed with the business owners
